mocks.title: Agent Ticket Acquisition — headless interface mock
mocks.description: Headless agent acquires primary where we control the sale, secondary sealed bid where we don't — 1 seat vs 4 connected seats, Porto Alegre (route-1 primary) vs Miami (secondary only).
changelog: v1 — 2026-11-18: initial mock, built on the real commerce engine (commerce/engine.mjs); four cases self-asserted.
v2 — 2026-11-19: the venue app's human UI joins the sample as its preview — two faces: the human flow, and the agent underneath it.
mocks.objective: Prove the control doctrine in code: primary only where we are seller of record or technology partner; secondary sealed bid everywhere else — at 1-seat and 4-seat scale.
mocks.facesNote: This sample has two faces. The human flow is the venue ticketing experience: a person chooses a price area and how many seats must sit together, the allocating engine assigns the grouped seats, and the buyer accepts or declines — a primary sale where we are the seller of record, on the stadium example built around Internacional vs São Paulo at Beira-Rio. Underneath it sits the agent: the same acquisition run headlessly — primary only where we control the sale, secondary by sealed bid everywhere else, one seat or four connected, Porto Alegre primary against Miami secondary. One engine, two doors: people buy through the flow; agents buy through the interface.
